newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight at 6.60/70 pct after volatile swings.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight at 6.60/70 pct after volatile swings.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate in Kuala Lumpur was trading at 6.60/70 percent at around 0840 GMT after volatile swings, dealers said.
The rate was higher than late-Friday's 6.0 percent.
"It went to a high of 7.20 and then fall to 6.20. It's quite volatile," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.

Dealers said the volatility was quite natural when there was uncertainty on the most appropriate level for the overnight, the interest rate that banks charge one another on overnight loans. The volatility could also be due to mismatch of funds, they said.

They said the re-entry of festival funds into the banking system and recent flow of overseas money into Malaysia to take advantage of high interest rates have created some uncertainty on the levels of interbank rates.
Earlier, short-term interbank rates extended their fall due to inflow of market funds, dealers said.
Some three billion ringgit were expected to return into the system at the tail-end of the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr celebrations.
Dealers said one-week interbank rate was at 6.80/90 percent, down from 7.0 percent Friday. Two-week money was quoted at 7.00 from 7.10/20 and three-week at 7.00/20 against 7.20/25.
One-month rate was at 7.23/25 percent from 7.30/35 on Friday.
The three-month rate was at 7.30 from 7.30/35 and six-month to one-year were unchanged at 7.30/35.
